+# Flow 02: Sign in and session entry
+
+Status: initial draft; not approved  
+Date: 2026-10-22 (Asia/Qyzylorda)  
+Mode: specification only; no implementation or delivery evidence  
+Authority: [shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md), then the latest owner answers; retained [SPEC-001](../specifications/SPEC-001_dubbed_mvp.md) and [BR-001](../business-requirements/BR-001_custom_video_dubbing.md) apply only where the shared contract has not replaced them
+
+## 1. Purpose and boundary
+
+This flow lets a visitor authenticate with Google or an existing email/password identity, resolves the resulting account session, and enters the authenticated product.
+
+Confirmed boundaries:
+
+- sign-in occurs before any upload;
+- ordinary successful sign-in enters Flow 06 **New dub**;
+- **My projects** is available from authenticated navigation;
+- Flow 03 owns sign-up, email verification, and completion of email/password registration;
+- Flow 04 owns password reset;
+- Flow 05 owns explicit ownership-verified linking when Google and email/password identities use the same email;
+- an email match alone never authorizes linking, merging, or account replacement;
+- this flow does not create a project, upload media, reserve or spend credits, accept a recording, or start processing.
+
+The flow is bilingual in English and Russian and must work on desktop and phone. Exact routes, typeface, tokens, measurements, geometry, motion, session lifetime, credential-error disclosure, and protected-return behavior remain OPEN where identified below.
+
+## 2. Entry and exit
+
+### 2.1 Entry
+
+- **Sign in** from the public landing page.
+- **Start dubbing** from Flow 01 while anonymous, carrying the confirmed logical intent to enter New dub after authentication.
+- An unauthenticated attempt to enter an authenticated destination, carrying only validated safe return context.
+- A session-expired handoff from an authenticated flow; its final return destination is unresolved in Q2.
+- A return from Flow 03, Flow 04, or Flow 05 when that flow explicitly hands control back.
+- Browser reload, Back, or Forward while the sign-in or provider-return state is recoverable.
+
+No entry may carry raw video bytes, passwords, provider tokens, recording media, or a command to replay.
+
+### 2.2 Exit
+
+| State and action | Exit |
+|---|---|
+| Existing identity authenticates successfully from ordinary sign-in or Start dubbing | Flow 06 New dub. |
+| Existing authenticated session is resolved on entry | Flow 06 New dub, except a protected-session return governed by unresolved Q2. |
+| User chooses **Create account** | Flow 03 registration and verification. |
+| User chooses **Forgot password?** | Flow 04 password reset. |
+| Valid credentials belong to an unverified registration | Flow 03 verification handoff only if the disclosure behavior selected in Q3 permits it. |
+| Provider/account result requires identity linking | Flow 05 explicit ownership-verified linking. |
+| Google flow is cancelled | Return to the usable Flow 02 sign-in form without an authenticated session. |
+| User leaves sign-in | Return according to the valid prior navigation entry; do not fabricate a product destination. |
+
+Authentication success does not itself authorize upload, processing, purchase, account linking, or replay of the action that encountered an expired session.
+
+## 3. Design-skill application
+
+Both requested skills were read and applied as analysis constraints, not as owner approval:
+
+- `.agents/skills/design-taste-frontend/SKILL.md` and its app-screen/form guidance;
+- `.agents/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md`.
+
+Their relevant contribution is a sparse working form with one clear job, plain labels, one primary action, truthful pending/error states, visible focus, quiet flat surfaces, and a phone composition that preserves form order.
+
+The confirmed Dubbed direction overrides generated or randomly dealt styling:
+
+- white and light-gray surfaces with readable near-black text;
+- compact top navigation or authentication header, never a permanent sidebar;
+- flat controls without gradients, glows, glass, ornamental art, tinted icon tiles, or a marketing hero;
+- red only for actionable error semantics on this screen, and never as the only error signal;
+- no exact font, palette value, width, radius, spacing, breakpoint, or motion value is selected by this draft.
+
+No design draw, mockup, screenshot review, browser inspection, or runnable UI was produced.
+
+## 4. Screen anatomy
+
+### 4.1 Authentication header
+
+Required responsibilities:
+
+- Dubbed wordmark/home action;
+- English/Russian language control;
+- no account, project, credits, or upload controls before authentication is established;
+- no sidebar or empty application chrome around the form.
+
+Changing language updates labels, help, errors, provider status, and accessible names together. It must not clear typed email or password values. Initial locale and persistence follow the unresolved shared localization contract.
+
+### 4.2 Sign-in form
+
+Required controls in logical order:
+
+1. screen title: **Sign in** / **Войти**;
+2. Google action: **Continue with Google** / **Продолжить с Google**;
+3. a text separator whose accessible reading does not imply two simultaneous requirements;
+4. **Email** / **Электронная почта** field;
+5. **Password** / **Пароль** field;
+6. password show/hide control with a persistent accessible name and state;
+7. primary action: **Sign in** / **Войти**;
+8. **Forgot password?** / **Забыли пароль?**;
+9. **Create account** / **Создать аккаунт**.
+
+Labels remain visible above fields. Placeholders do not replace labels. Browser autofill, password managers, and paste must work. The form must not log, translate, persist in Zustand, or expose the password.
+
+No **Remember me** control may appear unless Q1 selects the explicit Remember-me option.
+
+### 4.3 Pending state
+
+- Disable duplicate submission for the active method while its request is pending.
+- Keep the form frame stable and expose a concise programmatic status.
+- Do not clear the email because of a transport failure.
+- Do not claim authentication, redirect success, or account ownership until the centralized service returns an authoritative result.
+- Google pending state may indicate that the user is continuing with the provider; it must not imitate a provider screen inside Dubbed.
+
+### 4.4 Credential and account-state feedback
+
+The public wording for wrong credentials, unverified registration, and verification help is unresolved in Q3.
+
+Regardless of the selected wording:
+
+- invalid email shape is associated with the email field before submission;
+- an empty password is associated with the password field;
+- authoritative credential failure does not clear either field automatically;
+- unverified registration does not become a completed account in Flow 02;
+- disabled, deleted, rate-limited, or unavailable account behavior must come from the future identity/security contract and must not be inferred here;
+- errors include text and programmatic association; color alone is insufficient.
+
+### 4.5 Google return state
+
+The provider-return surface resolves one authoritative outcome:
+
+- authenticated existing account;
+- cancelled by the user;
+- provider declined or returned an error;
+- callback/result invalid, stale, or unavailable;
+- explicit linking required through Flow 05;
+- temporarily unknown result requiring reconciliation.
+
+This draft does not select Google OAuth configuration, consent scopes, token handling, callback routes, proof rules, or provider-specific error disclosure.
+
+## 5. Main and alternate transitions
+
+### 5.1 Email/password success
+
+1. User enters email and password and activates **Sign in**.
+2. The client validates only field presence and the selected email-shape rule.
+3. The centralized identity service performs the authoritative credential check.
+4. On authenticated success, the client resolves the session and destination.
+5. Ordinary sign-in and Start dubbing enter Flow 06 New dub.
+6. A protected-session return follows Q2 and never automatically replays the interrupted action.
+
+### 5.2 Unverified registration
+
+1. The identity service identifies an existing email/password registration that is not complete because email verification has not succeeded.
+2. Flow 02 does not mark the account verified, issue welcome credits, or complete registration.
+3. The visible response and availability of a verification handoff depend on Q3.
+4. If the selected policy permits it, hand off to Flow 03 with opaque service-owned verification context; do not pass the password.
+
+### 5.3 Google success and same-email linking
+
+1. User activates **Continue with Google**.
+2. The centralized service starts the real provider interaction or a clearly labeled mock simulation.
+3. An existing already-linked identity may establish the session.
+4. If the provider identity conflicts with or matches an existing email/password identity that requires linking, do not merge automatically.
+5. Hand off to Flow 05 for explicit ownership verification.
+6. Flow 05 returns only after its own linking contract succeeds, is cancelled, or fails.
+
+### 5.4 Google cancellation and provider failure
+
+- Cancellation returns to the sign-in form with a concise non-success state and no session change.
+- Provider refusal, invalid callback, or temporary failure shows an actionable retry path without changing methods automatically.
+- A transport interruption after provider return is reconciled before starting another provider attempt.
+- Reload must not exchange or replay a completed callback blindly.
+- A mock must never be described as real Google consent, ownership proof, or provider availability.
+
+### 5.5 Registration and reset handoffs
+
+- **Create account** enters Flow 03; sign-in does not duplicate registration fields or verification UI.
+- **Forgot password?** enters Flow 04; sign-in does not send reset email or set a new password.
+- Only validated non-secret return context may follow these handoffs.
+- Successful return from either flow re-resolves the current session rather than trusting component memory.
+
+## 6. Session, reload, and protected-return behavior
+
+### 6.1 Session authority
+
+- The centralized session service is authoritative; Zustand may coordinate view state but is not the session record.
+- On reload or direct entry, resolve the session before presenting an authenticated destination as usable.
+- If resolution is unavailable, keep protected content inaccessible, show Retry, and do not relabel the user anonymous.
+- The session lifetime and persistence model remain blocked by Q1.
+
+### 6.2 Session expiry
+
+- When a protected operation discovers expiry, stop before any further protected mutation.
+- Preserve only safe context needed for a possible return; do not retain credentials or raw media in the auth route.
+- Sign-in success must not replay upload, processing, purchase, deletion, share, save, or recording acceptance.
+- The destination after successful reauthentication remains blocked by Q2.
+
+### 6.3 Product-state continuity
+
+Authentication must preserve the following confirmed ownership boundaries without claiming that Flow 02 stores the data:
+
+- account-owned unaccepted recording drafts are cross-device recoverable and have no inactivity expiry;
+- recovery offers an unaccepted draft without automatically accepting or replacing the current accepted take;
+- a validated upload left before processing is automatically preserved as a My projects draft and is not automatically processed on return;
+- project and draft retrieval occurs through their owning services after the authenticated account is resolved.
+
+Real cross-device recovery requires backend persistence. A frontend mock cannot prove it.
+
+## 7. Failure and recovery matrix
+
+| Condition | Required response |
+|---|---|
+| Invalid local field | Associate concise help with the first invalid field; no service call. |
+| Credential rejection | Use the wording policy selected in Q3; keep the form usable. |
+| Unverified registration | Remain incomplete; apply Q3 and hand off to Flow 03 only when allowed. |
+| Google cancelled | Return to sign-in; no error-styled blame and no session. |
+| Google/provider failure | Explain that sign-in could not complete; offer Retry and email/password. |
+| Linking required | Hand off to Flow 05; never merge by email match. |
+| Session resolution unavailable | Keep protected destinations closed; offer Retry. |
+| Session expires after sign-in | Stop the protected action and apply Q2 after reauthentication. |
+| Destination unavailable | Keep the authenticated session truthful and provide safe navigation; do not claim sign-in failed. |
+| Duplicate submission | One in-flight attempt per method; reconcile unknown outcomes before retry. |
+
+## 8. Desktop, phone, keyboard, and accessibility
+
+### Desktop
+
+- Use a compact authentication header and one narrow form column.
+- Keep title, provider action, fields, errors, and handoff links in one reading order.
+- Do not place promotional cards, testimonials, security illustrations, or product screenshots beside the form.
+
+### Phone
+
+- Use one vertical sequence with no horizontal page scroll.
+- Keep outer margins, form width, and exact breakpoints OPEN under the shared design contract.
+- Interactive targets must meet the selected accessibility target-size standard; 44px is the current design target, not an approved token.
+- The software keyboard must not cover the active field, its error, or the primary action.
+- Long Russian labels may wrap without truncation or overlap.
+
+### Keyboard and assistive technology
+
+- Order: header, title, Google action, separator, email, password, show/hide, primary action, reset, registration.
+- Enter submits the eligible email/password form; it never starts Google sign-in.
+- Visible focus is required for every interactive control.
+- On local validation failure, focus the first invalid field and associate its message programmatically.
+- Pending, failure, provider return, and authenticated success are announced without repeated focus theft.
+- Show/hide changes exposure state without changing the password value or moving focus.
+- Language switching updates the document language and accessible names without clearing fields.
+
+## 9. Logical service boundary
+
+Names describe responsibilities, not approved endpoints, libraries, or implementation files.
+
+| Logical operation | Inputs | Required result categories |
+|---|---|---|
+| `resolveSession` | Current browser/session context | authenticated account summary, anonymous, expired, unavailable |
+| `signInWithPassword` | Email, password, locale, opaque validated return context | authenticated, credential/account response governed by Q3, rate limited, unavailable |
+| `startGoogleSignIn` | Locale, opaque validated return context | provider handoff, unavailable |
+| `resolveGoogleReturn` | Provider-owned return context | authenticated, cancelled, failed, linking required, unknown/unavailable |
+| `resolvePostAuthDestination` | Authenticated session plus validated logical intent | New dub for ordinary sign-in/Start dubbing; Q2 result for expired-session return; invalid/unavailable |
+
+The future implementation must keep backend/provider calls behind one centralized interchangeable service boundary. The specification does not approve a particular auth SDK or security protocol.
+
+## 10. Mock-truth boundary
+
+An interchangeable mock may deterministically simulate:
+
+- anonymous, authenticated, expired, pending, and unavailable session states;
+- password success, credential rejection, unverified registration, rate limit, and service failure;
+- Google success, cancellation, provider failure, linking-required, and unknown callback outcomes;
+- the three destination policies under Q2 for UI testing only.
+
+A mock cannot prove:
+
+- real Google consent, token exchange, provider identity, or mailbox ownership;
+- password storage, hashing, transport protection, credential-stuffing resistance, or account-enumeration resistance;
+- session cookie security, revocation, expiry, cross-browser continuity, or the policy selected in Q1;
+- explicit ownership proof or safe account merging in Flow 05;
+- backend-owned project or recording-draft recovery across devices.
+
+Mock checks must be labeled simulation rather than authentication, provider, backend, or security evidence.
+
+## 11. Visible copy and localization
+
+Baseline labels are specified in section 4. Final EN/RU copy requires editorial review.
+
+Copy rules:
+
+- use **Sign in** consistently for the email/password action and resulting status;
+- use **Continue with Google** for the provider action;
+- do not say **Account created** or **Email verified** in this flow;
+- do not say identities were linked until Flow 05 confirms success;
+- provider failures name the failed action and the next available action without exposing technical tokens;
+- the selected Q3 policy must be equivalent in EN and RU, including what it reveals about account and verification state;
+- no locale may expose more account-existence information than the other.
+
+## 12. Acceptance criteria
+
+| ID | Acceptance criterion | Status |
+|---|---|---|
+| F02-AC01 | A visitor can sign in through an existing Google or email/password identity from desktop and phone in EN and RU. | Confirmed behavior; requires implementation evidence. |
+| F02-AC02 | Ordinary successful sign-in and Start dubbing enter Flow 06 New dub before any upload begins. | Confirmed. |
+| F02-AC03 | Create account and Forgot password hand off to Flow 03 and Flow 04 without duplicating their responsibilities. | Confirmed. |
+| F02-AC04 | An unverified email/password registration cannot complete in Flow 02. | Confirmed; visible behavior BLOCKED by Q3. |
+| F02-AC05 | Same-email Google/password identities never link or merge without Flow 05 explicit ownership verification. | Confirmed. |
+| F02-AC06 | Google cancellation, provider failure, invalid/unknown return, and linking-required states preserve truthful session state and usable recovery. | Confirmed behavior; real provider evidence pending. |
+| F02-AC07 | Session reload is resolved from the centralized service and component memory cannot establish authentication. | Confirmed behavior; real service evidence pending. |
+| F02-AC08 | Session persistence, expiry, and any Remember-me control match one owner-selected policy. | BLOCKED by Q1. |
+| F02-AC09 | Reauthentication after expiry reaches the owner-selected destination without replaying the interrupted protected action. | BLOCKED by Q2. |
+| F02-AC10 | Credential rejection and unverified-registration feedback match one disclosure policy in equivalent EN/RU copy. | BLOCKED by Q3. |
+| F02-AC11 | The form supports keyboard order, Enter behavior, visible focus, associated errors, announced status, autofill/password managers, paste, and non-color-only feedback. | Confirmed behavior; evidence pending. |
+| F02-AC12 | The rendered screen uses the light white/gray flat direction, compact top header, and no permanent sidebar, gradient, glow, or decorative auth art. | BLOCKED by approved shared tokens and rendered visual review. |
+| F02-AC13 | Sign-in never creates a project, uploads media, spends credits, starts processing, accepts a take, or auto-processes a recovered validated-upload draft. | Confirmed. |
+| F02-AC14 | Mock evidence is reported as simulation and never as Google, backend, cross-device, session-security, or account-linking proof. | Confirmed. |
+
+## 13. Verification plan — not executed
+
+No product check was run for this specification. After implementation and the blocked decisions exist, verify:
+
+1. State tests for anonymous/authenticated/expired/unavailable sessions; password success/rejection/unverified/rate-limit/unavailable; Google success/cancel/failure/linking-required/unknown.
+2. Transition tests for landing Sign in, Start dubbing, direct sign-in, Flow 03/04/05 handoffs, already-authenticated entry, session expiry, and invalid destination context.
+3. Non-replay checks proving that upload, processing, purchase, deletion, sharing, save, and recording acceptance do not run automatically after authentication.
+4. Reload/Back/Forward checks during password pending, provider handoff/return, unknown result reconciliation, success, and expired-session return.
+5. Credential-handling review proving passwords do not enter persisted Zustand state, logs, analytics, URLs, visible diagnostics, or localization payloads.
+6. Keyboard-only and assistive-technology review for focus order, Enter behavior, validation focus, show/hide state, provider status, live announcements, and language switching.
+7. Responsive visual review at representative desktop and 390px phone widths after shared tokens are approved; inspect long Russian copy, zoom/reflow, keyboard occlusion, clipping, and target sizes.
+8. Integration checks with real Google and backend identity/session services for callback reconciliation, linking handoff, session persistence/expiry, and cross-device session behavior. These cannot be proven by the current specification or a mock.
+9. Cross-flow data checks that authenticated account resolution retrieves My projects and account-owned drafts without Flow 02 accepting, processing, or mutating them.
+
+Record procedure or command, result, environment, date, revision/dirty-tree boundary, fixture/account class, and evidence location. Mark simulated and unavailable dependencies explicitly.
+
+## 14. Dependencies
+
+- [Shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md)
+- [Flow 01 landing](01-landing.md)
+- Flow 03 registration and email verification
+- [Flow 04 password reset](04-password-reset.md)
+- Flow 05 explicit account linking
+- [Flow 06 New dub](06-new-dub.md)
+- [Flow 11 My projects](11-projects.md)
+- centralized identity, session, localization, navigation-intent, project, and draft services
+- real Google provider configuration and production backend identity/session implementation
+- approved shared authentication tokens, typography, geometry, focus treatment, and responsive composition
+
+## 15. Open decisions
+
+The following three questions were already submitted to the Orchestrator and remain unanswered. They are reproduced to preserve their IDs and state; this draft does not recommend or select an option.
+
+| ID | Unselected options | Blocks |
+|---|---|---|
+| Q1 — Session persistence | A: 30-day sliding session. B: session lasts until the browser closes. C: explicit **Remember me**, with a 30-day session when selected. | Session lifetime, reload/reopen behavior, Remember-me anatomy, F02-AC08. |
+| Q2 — Return after session expiry | A: return to the last safe protected view without replaying the interrupted action. B: always enter New dub. C: enter My projects. | Protected return intent, reauthentication destination, F02-AC09. |
+| Q3 — Email/password error policy | A: common **Incorrect email or password** for invalid credentials, while valid credentials for an unverified registration show the verification handoff. B: neutral copy for all failures. C: a verification-help-link policy. | Account-state disclosure, verification handoff, EN/RU error copy, F02-AC04/F02-AC10. |
+
+No default is implied by option order. Auth/session lifetime, error-leak policy, and post-expiry user-intent routing remain unapproved until the owner answers through the Orchestrator.
*** End Patch";
const r = await tools.apply_patch(patch);
text(r);
